video_title: This SUPER FAST 2.0 Log Bait Cycle is BUSTED!!

Hero variant (Savage Survival, 3 elixir): the ability is attempted exactly once and does not fire — "Can I ability here? Aw, the ability didn't get off. But, that's fine. It's still a connection" (1091-1095s), with his elixir reading 2-3 at that moment.
royal-hogs: The opponent's win condition, split down both lanes at clock 2:35, 1:43-1:35 and 0:17. Ryley's standing answer is Cannon centrally plus Skeletons plus a spirit — "Let's go for the cannon then skellies. He might fireball that. Yeah, let's go for the ice spirit here" (941-946s), and the clock 1:33 version costs him almost nothing: "beautiful defense taking almost no damage outside of the fireball" (952-956s).

He keeps expecting them in overtime and plays around them rather than pre-empting — "He might go for the piggies" (1061s), "He might go for a piggies though, so I have to be very very cautious" (1042-1046s).

clock 1:11: he credits a fast defensive gang — "He's going to have to go for the Goblin Gang. That could be full countered. Yeah, that was a good gang by him. He was very fast with that. I have to give him credit there" (968-974s).

He plays his Dart Goblin around it — "Don't want to give him any fireball value this time" (940s) — and treats every wasted one as free cycle: "Every time he wastes fireball, I can just cycle a free cannon to be honest" (1116-1119s).
the-log: clock 1:25: taken as the answer to the Wall Breakers instead of Goblin Gang — "He can't even really gang. It would be too late... he had the log instead" (958-961s).

It shapes two of his placements: the Goblin Barrel thrown to draw it out ("Let's barrel as well to force out the log", 990s) and the Dart Goblin placed low ("we can go for the low Dark Goblin outside of the range of the log", 995-997s).
freeze: clock 1:16 (t=1085.1, tile [11, 6]): the opponent freezes his defence and kills the Cannon. Ryley writes it off immediately because the Evo Dart Goblin survives — "He did get our cannon, but it's fine. Our Dark Elixir is just putting in so much work" (1084-1090s).
clone: Tracked twice on the opponent's side near the right bridge (t=1059.1 tile [14, 15] at clock 1:43, t=1107.1 tile [14, 17] at clock 0:54). Ryley never names the card; at the second one he reacts to an animation he cannot place — "He's going to use ability, bro. What? I mean, I guess it worked, but that was still interesting" (1107-1112s), so the Clone reads come from the detector rather than from commentary.

bullets: Game 6 of 7 in a single-deck ladder session (video 872.0-1136.1s); the 2.0-elixir Log Bait cycle of the video title, with Evolutions on Goblin Barrel, Wall Breakers and Dart Goblin and the Heroic Berserker (Savage Survival). Against a Royal Hogs bait/cycle deck (Firecracker, Evo Bats, Goblin Gang, Fireball, The Log, Freeze, Clone) that he identifies as "that piggy's princess deck" (901s).

The offensive pattern is one package repeated: split Wall Breakers plus Evo Goblin Barrel with Electro Spirit or Ice Spirit on top, run at clock 1:58, 1:27, 0:54-0:48, 0:29-0:27, 0:12 and through the whole of overtime — "the E-Spirit plus wall breakers again for like the millionth time" (1103-1107s). Enemy right tower 4724 -> 3255 HP at clock 1:57-1:48; enemy left tower 4858 -> 1085 HP at clock 0:48-0:47.

Defence is Cannon centrally ([8, 10], [8, 9], [9, 11], [9, 10]) plus Skeletons plus a one-elixir spirit against Royal Hogs, with the Berserker as the finishing body and king activation as a stated goal — "Just make sure we activate the king and beautiful defense taking almost no damage outside of the fireball" (951-956s).

Placement rules he states for the deck against a spell/Log list: Dart Goblin deep and wide so it is safe from Fireball and Log ([15, 4], [9, 5], [2, 7]) — "Don't want to give him any fireball value this time" (940s), "the low Dark Goblin outside of the range of the log" (995s) — and Berserker down before Wall Breakers whenever Goblin Gang is up (1033-1036s).

The game goes to overtime at t=1044 (the first overtime of the session: "Not a single one of our matches so far has actually went to overtime", 872-880s), and the cycle is what wins it — "this guy's just struggling to keep up with our cycle" (1077-1080s) and "Every time he wastes fireball, I can just cycle a free cannon to be honest" (1116-1119s). Closed at clock 0:35: "The barrel and that is good game. Let's go. Beautiful win, man" (1126-1130s). Win.

new_deck.rationale: Evolved Goblin Barrel and Wall Breakers are played to bait out The Log and the opponent's swarm, and at 2.0 average elixir the deck cycles back to them faster than any answer can be recycled.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: Every card is a bait or a cycle card: Goblin Barrel and Wall Breakers force the small spell, Skeletons, Ice Spirit and Electro Spirit cost one elixir each so the barrel comes back almost immediately, and Cannon plus Berserker hold the ground while that happens. Ryley pilots it as a pressure loop rather than as a single big push — split Wall Breakers on one side, barrel on the other, a spirit on top, then straight back to defence. The two placement rules he repeats are keeping the Evolved Dart Goblin out of Fireball and Log range and putting the Berserker down before the Wall Breakers whenever the opponent has a swarm in cycle. Its edge in a long game is elixir economy: each wasted opponent Fireball buys a free Cannon, and by overtime the opponent "can't keep up with our cycle". The stated weakness is a Princess-style ranged unit it cannot kill — "princess is super good against my deck ... I'm just completely unable to kill it" (916-921s).
